phase2_distribution.pathway: B: rainfall-distribution models from the raw ensemble

emos_csg.name: EMOS, censored shifted gamma
emos_csg.estimates: rainfall distribution with a probability of zero
emos_csg.predictors: ensemble mean m' and mean absolute difference md' (relative)

extended_logistic.name: Heteroscedastic extended logistic regression
extended_logistic.predictors: sqrt of the ensemble mean m', log spread s' (relative)
extended_logistic.fitting: log loss over each cell’s CHIRPS deciles, pooled

quantile_regression.name: Regularized quantile regression
quantile_regression.estimates: conditional quantiles at 19 levels (5–95%), CDF by interpolation
quantile_regression.predictors: ensemble mean m' and spread s' (relative)
quantile_regression.fitting: pinball loss per level (Huber-smoothed), L2 1e-4, pooled

references.incumbent: MVS -> smoothed counts -> climatology blend (published probabilities)

emos_csg.form: mu = softplus(a0 + a1 m), sigma = softplus(b0 + b1 md), delta = -softplus(d)

extended_logistic.thresholds: training CHIRPS deciles of each cell

quantile_regression.tails: linear to 0 below the lowest level; linear to 1 at q_max + (q_max - q_0.5) above the highest

config_contents.description: Phase 3, Pathway B: Bayesian joint probability, BMA for precipitation and quantile regression forests from the raw ensemble against the published pipeline (docs/48).

phase3.pathway: B: rainfall-distribution models from the raw ensemble

bjp.name: Bayesian joint probability
bjp.estimates: rainfall distribution (log-sinh normal, censored at zero, Student-t predictive)
bjp.fitting: censored maximum likelihood of the transforms and the joint normal; parameter uncertainty integrated with the number of training years as the effective sample

bma_precipitation.name: Bayesian model averaging for precipitation
bma_precipitation.estimates: mixture over members: probability of zero and a gamma for the cube root of the amount
bma_precipitation.predictors: each member's amount f' (relative), equal weights for exchangeable members
bma_precipitation.fitting: maximum likelihood of the mixture, pooled

quantile_regression_forest.name: Quantile regression forest
quantile_regression_forest.estimates: conditional distribution as leaf-weighted training amounts; quantiles at 39 levels (2.5–97.5%)
quantile_regression_forest.predictors: m', s', md', ensemble 10% and 90% quantiles (relative), log climatological mean, CHIRPS coefficient of variation
quantile_regression_forest.fitting: 200 trees, at least 40 samples per leaf, half the predictors per split, pooled

references.incumbent: MVS -> smoothed counts -> climatology blend (published probabilities)

bma_precipitation.form: logit P0 = a0 + a1 f^(1/3) + a2 1{f=0}; Y^(1/3)|Y>0 ~ Gamma(mean softplus(b0 + b1 f^(1/3)), variance softplus(c0) + softplus(c1) f)

quantile_regression_forest.weights: all training samples of each leaf, by sample weight (Meinshausen 2006)

shadow_config.description: Shadow rainfall-amount and range forecast from a rainfall-distribution model (scripts/dist_shadow.py, docs/48). Cycles are matched by initialization month and season, so future cycle files are covered without editing this file. Shadow forecasts are never published as forecasts; the published probabilities and amounts are unchanged. Besides the configured model (EMOS), every distribution model the method selection (scripts/method_selection.py) lists as a candidate for a cycle gets its own shadow, so its independent validation seasons accumulate.
shadow_config.reason: In Phase 2 the EMOS 10-90% intervals held 76-84% of observed totals where the MVS-corrected ensemble's held 46-76% (80% is calibrated), and EMOS was confirmed better in CRPS for the January-initialized FMAM season and JJAS September. The shadow builds independent evidence season by season before any amount or range product is considered.
